extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Greek art, art historians, museum visitors, and those learning to criticise classical sculpture
extracted.subtask_description: How to read and criticise Greek sculpture from the Heroic Age: guidance for connecting surviving works to their original materials, minor arts, literary context, and viewing conditions so as to recover their full meaning and sensuous effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual approach: intellectual and sensuous
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete criticism must have approached them from both sides--from the side of the intelligence... but from the sensuous side also.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess Greek sculpture both as embodiments of thought (its intellectual content, narrative or conceptual design) and as sensuous material objects (form, surface, visual effect). Do not privilege only abstract interpretation; attend equally to what the works 'address' to the eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnect sculpture with the minor arts and material culture
rubrics_metrics.description: To have this really Greek sense of Greek sculpture, it is necessary to connect it... with the minor works of price, intaglios, coins, vases; with that whole system of material refinement and beauty in the outer Greek life, which these minor works represent to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a major sculpture, situate it within the broader craft tradition (metal-work, ivories, textiles, vases, small-scale objects). Use surviving minor arts as a complementary background to restore the object's original atmosphere and social/material context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-intellectualising the sculptor's practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek sculpture has come to be regarded as the product of a peculiarly limited art... He is fancied to have been disdainful of such matters as the mere tone, the fibre or texture of his marble or cedar-wood...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the sculptor as concerned only with abstract form; criticism should not erase evidence of craft choices, material sensitivity, or tactile concerns. Attend to the artist's handling of material as an integral part of meaning and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover original materials and polychromy mentally
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole black and grey world of extant antique sculpture needing to be translated back into ivory and gold, if we would feel the excitement which the Greek seems to have felt in the presence of these objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for lost colour, added precious materials (ivory, gold, metal attachments), and original surface treatments when judging appearance and impact. Museums' bare marble can falsify the original sensory experience; mentally restore likely polychromy and metal elements where evidence allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct original architectural and environmental setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek sculpture is presented to us in such falsifying isolation... isolation, secondly, from the architectural group of which... that frieze, for instance, was designed to be a part; isolation, thirdly, from the clear Greek skies, the poetical Greek life, in our modern galleries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works with attention to their intended placement (temple frieze, pediment, cult image), viewing distances and angles, and outdoor/in situ lighting. Consider how separation from that context in museums alters perception and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use literary sources (Homer) to inform reconstruction of the Heroic Age
rubrics_metrics.description: Of this period we possess, indeed, no direct history... but as to its whole character and outward local colouring, for its art... Homer may be regarded as an authority. The Iliad and the Odyssey... represent it as already delighting itself in the application of precious material and skilful handiwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material evidence is scarce, incorporate literary descriptions (e.g., Homeric passages) to infer aesthetic priorities, subjects, and techniques of early Greek art. Treat such sources critically but as valuable guides to cultural attitudes toward decoration and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance appreciation of formal design with sensitivity to craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The works of the highest Greek sculpture are indeed intellectualised... yet, though the most abstract and intellectualised of sensuous objects, they are still sensuous and material, addressing themselves, in the first instance, not to the purely reflective faculty, but to the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluation, credit the sculptor's design and conceptual achievement while also registering the 'pure skill of hand'—proportions, finish, textural finesse—that produces immediate visual pleasure. Both aspects are necessary to understand the work's greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek the 'proper atmosphere' for authentic response
rubrics_metrics.description: If one... endeavours mentally to throw them back into that proper atmosphere, through which alone they can exercise over us all the magic by which they charmed their original spectators, the effort is not always a successful one, within the grey walls of the Louvre or the British Museum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and viewers should attempt—wherever possible mentally or through reconstruction—to re-place sculptures in their historical, ritual, and environmental contexts (lighting, ritual use, colour, associated objects) to approximate the original emotional and aesthetic impact.
